AI & Cybersecurity · Part B01 / 40

Teaching aim: distinguish AI used for cybersecurity, malicious use of AI, attacks against AI systems, and broader AI safety concerns. No coding or mathematics required. Suggested pacing: 70–90 minutes or two class meetings. Evidence includes primary sources published through September 2026. The server-room photograph is illustrative.

Photo: Florian Hirzinger. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:CERN_Server_03.jpg. CC BY-SA 3.0. Image fitted or cropped for placement.

Opening scenario

A familiar voice asks for help

🔊 Voice message · sounds like your cousin“I’m in trouble. Send money now. Please don’t call.”

What makes it persuasive? A familiar voice, fear, urgency — and a request not to check.

A convincing voice is evidence to check, not proof of identity.

What do you do first?

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B02 / 40

Interactive: Fictional scenario based on a documented fraud category (FBI IC3, Dec 2024). Let the room vote before clicking.

Fictional scenario based on a documented category of fraud. Ask students to separate the emotional request from identity verification. Useful responses include calling the person through a known number or contacting a trusted person. Do not rely on detecting tiny audio flaws because synthesized voices may be convincing.

FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center. Criminals Use Generative Artificial Intelligence to Facilitate Financial Fraud (3 December 2024). https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2024/PSA241203

Foundations

Cybersecurity and AI safety overlap

Cybersecurity
Can someone steal, disrupt, manipulate, or misuse a system?
AI safety
Can an AI system cause unacceptable harm through its behavior or use?
Overlap
Can an attacker make an AI agent take a harmful action?

Safety also includes harmful failures without an attacker.

Where does it belong?

Ransomware locks an AI company’s serversSecurity: an attacker disrupts a system — the AI is incidental.
A chatbot confidently gives wrong advice, no attacker involvedSafety: harmful behavior without an adversary.
Hidden text on a web page makes an agent delete filesBoth: an attacker steers an AI system into a harmful action.
An agent pursues a badly specified goal and closes real requestsSafety: a specification failure (more on slide 30).
AI & Cybersecurity · Part B03 / 40

These are working definitions for the class, not a claim of universal agreement on terminology. Security often emphasizes adversarial threats. AI safety also covers accidental failures, misuse, and potential loss of control. Privacy, fairness, and accountability are related dimensions of trustworthy AI.

NIST. AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (2023) and framework resources. https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework

Capability and exposure

Why concern is increasing

Capability

Capability

Predict, then click.

Models can perform more demanding software and information tasks.

Access

Access

Predict, then click.

Useful capabilities reach more people and organizations.

Autonomy

Autonomy

Predict, then click.

Connected agents can turn suggestions into actions.

Dependence

Dependence

Predict, then click.

Failures matter more as people rely on AI in consequential work.

Risk also depends on deployment, access, safeguards, and who may be harmed. Better benchmark scores do not translate directly into a fixed increase in real-world harm.

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B05 / 40

This is a qualitative synthesis. Increasing capability can support both protection and misuse. Risk also depends on deployment conditions, access, safeguards, and who may be harmed. Avoid assuming that model benchmark improvements translate directly into a fixed increase in real-world harm.

Bengio et al. International AI Safety Report 2026, Extended Summary for Policymakers (3 February 2026). Evidence synthesis, not a prediction consensus. https://internationalaisafetyreport.org/publication/2026-report-extended-summary-policymakers

Reading AI risk claims

Three kinds of evidence

Observed incident
Something happened in a real setting. Scope may still be uncertain.
Controlled experiment
A behavior occurred under stated test conditions.
Future scenario
A plausible pathway, with uncertain likelihood.

The label should stay attached when the claim gets repeated.

Label each claim

The FBI warns of AI-generated videos impersonating its staff (2026)Observed incident: a real-world warning.
Researchers build a fictional company and watch how models behaveControlled experiment: designed conditions.
Advanced systems might one day resist correctionFuture scenario: a pathway, not an observation.
A provider reports actors using agents against several victimsObserved incident — seen from one company’s view.
AI & Cybersecurity · Part B06 / 40

Interactive: This label recurs all deck long. Students keep it for the exit ticket.

Use an example: a reported deepfake fraud is an incident, a simulated agent deception test is an experiment, and a future loss-of-control pathway is a scenario. Company telemetry can reveal real misuse while leaving gaps about victims or outcomes. Strong communication preserves those limits. This evidence framework is an original teaching aid.

Defending with AI

AI has helped filter threats for years

Learning patterns in large volumes of data.

Machine learning can flag spam, suspicious behavior, and malware that deserve attention.

The prediction still needs a useful response.

A filter scores 60 messages · ■ scam · ● real

Simulated scores · illustrative volumes

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B07 / 40

Interactive: Slide the threshold down: more scams caught, and the false-alarm pile explodes. Slide it up: quiet, but scams slip through. A prediction is a judgment under uncertainty.

Generative AI did not introduce all AI use in cybersecurity. Earlier machine-learning methods classified messages and other signals. Explain that a prediction is a judgment under uncertainty. A detector that produces many alerts can still fail operationally if the team cannot investigate them.

Google Research. Federated Learning: Collaborative Machine Learning without Centralized Training Data (2017), discusses training Gmail spam filters. https://research.google/blog/federated-learning-collaborative-machine-learning-without-centralized-training-data/

Defending with AI

The analyst’s assistant

Useful work

An assistant can summarize alerts and help an analyst understand unfamiliar evidence.

Necessary check

The analyst needs the original logs, and a clear line between evidence and AI inference.

Same incident

“Between 02:10 and 02:14, account jdoe signed in from a new country, then downloaded 3 GB. This is likely an attacker using stolen credentials.”

The highlighted sentence is an inference, not evidence.

02:10:03  login ok   user=jdoe  ip=203.0.113.7  geo=new
02:10:41  mfa ok     user=jdoe  method=push
02:12:15  download   user=jdoe  size=1.4GB
02:13:58  download   user=jdoe  size=1.6GB

The MFA approval is in the log. Was it jdoe traveling, or a tired click on a push prompt? The log alone does not say.

Discuss

What would let the analyst challenge a wrong summary?

Links back to the source records, time stamps, and a stated level of uncertainty. Confident prose without those is harder to check than the raw log.
AI & Cybersecurity · Part B08 / 40

Interactive: Fictional log using documentation IP addresses. Photo credit for the original slide: Benjamin le Roux / Unsplash.

A log is a record of events generated by a system. Present this as a possible workflow, not a guarantee about a specific product. Ask what information would let an analyst challenge an incorrect summary. Sources, time stamps, and uncertainty statements are more useful than confident prose alone.

Documented research

AI-assisted vulnerability repair

Found
54

unique synthetic vulnerabilities in the 2025 final

Challenges
63

in the final round

Example
DARPA’s AI Cyber Challenge tested automated discovery and patching.
Context
A defined test environment with planted flaws.
Caution
Success there does not guarantee safe repair of every real system.

What does this result establish?

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B09 / 40

DARPA reported the final results on August 8, 2025. Competitors found 54 unique synthetic vulnerabilities in 63 final challenges. Synthetic means organizers deliberately inserted them for evaluation. Explain a patch as a software change intended to fix a problem. Mention that functional correctness and regressions matter as well as removing a weakness.

DARPA. AI Cyber Challenge marks pivotal inflection point for cyber defense (8 August 2025). Competition results. https://www.darpa.mil/news/2025/aixcc-results

Defense trade-off

A fast response can still be wrong

Useful automation

Flag a suspicious login and collect supporting evidence.

Consequential action

Disable an account or interrupt a critical service.

The level of review should reflect the possible harm.

At 2 a.m., a hospital system raises an alert. Automate, or ask a person?

Collect the related logs into one case fileAutomate: low risk, easy to undo, saves time.
Add a warning banner to a suspicious emailAutomate: reversible and low harm.
Disable a clinician’s account in the middle of a shiftAsk a person: a false alarm could delay care.
Shut down the patient-scheduling serviceAsk a person — unless waiting is clearly worse. Urgency, reversibility and operational need decide.
AI & Cybersecurity · Part B10 / 40

Interactive: Hypothetical scenario. Not every action always requires manual approval.

Use a hypothetical false alarm on a hospital employee account. Some low-risk steps can proceed automatically, while disruptive actions may require a stronger check. The appropriate design depends on urgency, reversibility, and operational needs. Do not imply that every action always requires a manual approval. This is an original scenario.

Malicious use

AI can make deception easier to produce

Language

Language

Predict, then click.

Messages can sound polished in many languages.

Personalization

Personalization

Predict, then click.

Public information can help tailor a persuasive story.

Media

Media

Predict, then click.

Synthetic audio or video can support impersonation.

Volume

Volume

Predict, then click.

Automation can reduce the effort per attempted scam.

The mechanism is still manipulation of trust. Polished does not mean AI-made, and AI is not needed for these crimes.

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B11 / 40

FBI guidance describes criminals using generative AI to create persuasive text and synthetic media. Do not claim all polished messages are AI-generated or that AI is necessary for these crimes. The central mechanism remains manipulation of trust.

FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center. Criminals Use Generative Artificial Intelligence to Facilitate Financial Fraud (3 December 2024). https://www.ic3.gov/PSA/2024/PSA241203

Malicious use

AI assistance in cyber operations

Step 1

Preparation

Explain unfamiliar technology and organize information.

Step 2

Development

Help write or revise software.

Step 3

Execution

Assist repeated tasks through connected tools.

Step 4

Interpretation

Process results and suggest what to examine next.

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B13 / 40

Keep this at a conceptual level. NCSC’s May 2025 assessment forecasts that AI will make elements of intrusion operations more effective and efficient through 2027. A forecast is not a count of successful attacks. Domain expertise, access, operational constraints, and defensive measures still affect outcomes.

UK NCSC. Impact of AI on cyber threat from now to 2027 (7 May 2025). Forward-looking assessment. https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/report/impact-ai-cyber-threat-now-2027

Reported incidents

Agentic misuse in a 2026 threat report

Source
Anthropic’s September 2026 report on malicious uses found on its platform.
Pattern
Some actors used agent frameworks across multiple victims.
Human role
People still selected targets and reviewed important results.
Limit
One provider’s view is not the whole threat landscape.

Does the report support this headline?

“Some criminals used AI agents against several victims”Supported, attributed to Anthropic.
“Humans still chose the targets”Supported: target selection, monetization and review stayed with people.
“AI attacks are now fully autonomous”Not supported. The report describes different levels of autonomy.
“This is the complete count of AI-enabled attacks”Not supported. It is one company’s first-party investigation.
AI & Cybersecurity · Part B14 / 40

Attribute every claim here to Anthropic. The report describes multiple operations and different levels of autonomy. It says humans retained decisions including target selection, monetization, and review. This is a company’s first-party investigation, not an independently complete census of AI-enabled attacks. Do not describe the activity as universally autonomous.

Anthropic. Countering misuse of AI: September 2026. First-party threat report. https://www.anthropic.com/threat-intelligence-report-september-2026

Evidence limits

Demonstrated capability and real-world risk

A test can show

A model can carry out a task under specified conditions.

An incident adds

Evidence about access, intent, and actual effects.

Risk assessments need both capability and deployment context.

A model solves a hacking challenge in a lab network. Which detail matters most for judging real-world risk?

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B15 / 40

Use the contrast between a laboratory network and an unfamiliar production environment. Experiments can expose dangerous possibilities before harm occurs. Incidents can reveal how people really use systems. Neither alone settles future risk. Explain that a test result should include what tools, information, and time the system received.

Anthropic. Cyber toolkits for LLMs (13 June 2025). Controlled cybersecurity research. https://www.anthropic.com/research/cyber-toolkits

Pair discussion · 3 minutes

Who benefits from the same capability?

An AI system finds a software weakness quickly.

  1. How could a defender use that result?
  2. How could a malicious actor misuse it?
  3. What determines which side gains more?
Pair time
Debrief

What tips the balance?

Who has access to the capability first, how fast fixes are deployed, how flaws are disclosed, and the incentives on each side. Defenders must fix everything; attackers need one gap.

The same capability can support very different outcomes.

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B16 / 40

Interactive: Keep the discussion high-level; no exploit procedures.

Allow three minutes. Expected discussion: defenders can repair or prioritize exposure, while attackers may exploit it. Relative advantage depends on deployment coverage, vulnerability disclosure, speed of remediation, and system access. Keep the discussion high-level and avoid describing exploit procedures. This is a conceptual exercise.

Protecting AI

The AI system has more than a model

Click a component. Then: which one should enforce a limit on reading private records?

A secure model alone cannot guarantee a secure application.

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B17 / 40

Interactive: Answer to the closing question: authorization controls in the account and data layers (A and E), not a written instruction to the model.

The connector photograph illustrates integration. Distinguish the model from the application that supplies context, grants access, and executes actions. Ask which component should enforce a limit on reading private records. The answer should point to authorization controls, not only a written instruction to the model.

NIST. AI 100-2 E2025: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations (2025). https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/ai/100/2/e2025/final

Protecting AI

Prompt injection

Untrusted content tries to become an instruction.

Task“Summarize this email for me.”

Hi! Notes from Tuesday’s meeting are below…
[hidden text: tells the assistant to send the user’s files to an outside address]

The risk grows when the assistant has useful access and tools.

Turn defenses on and off

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B18 / 40

Interactive: Start with all off, then turn on only the first box: the odds improve but nothing guarantees it. Then add either app control. No operational payload is shown.

An indirect prompt injection arrives through material the assistant reads while performing a legitimate task. It can compete with the user’s intended instruction. Do not provide an operational payload. Explain the general problem as confusion between data and authority. NCSC notes that this problem differs from conventional injection vulnerabilities.

UK NCSC. Prompt injection is not SQL injection (it may be worse). https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/blog-post/prompt-injection-is-not-sql-injection

Related terms

Jailbreak and prompt injection

Jailbreak
A user tries to get a model past its intended restrictions.
Prompt injection
Untrusted input tries to redirect the application’s intended behavior.
Overlap
An injection can use techniques that also bypass restrictions.

Boundaries vary across research and industry.

Which is it, mainly?

A user keeps rephrasing to get around a refusalJailbreak: the user is the one pushing.
A web page the agent reads tells it to forward the user’s filesPrompt injection: the instruction arrives through content.
A shared document hides text that redirects a summarizerPrompt injection, through a different doorway.
A user invents a role-play to unlock forbidden contentJailbreak.
AI & Cybersecurity · Part B19 / 40

Use these as practical distinctions, not mutually exclusive formal categories. A direct malicious user prompt and a malicious instruction hidden in retrieved material enter through different trust relationships. Application defenses should account for both.

NIST. AI 100-2 E2025: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations (2025). https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/ai/100/2/e2025/final

UK NCSC. Prompt injection is not SQL injection (it may be worse). https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/blog-post/prompt-injection-is-not-sql-injection

Protecting AI

Sensitive information can leak

User input
People paste private information into a service.
Retrieval
The app may fetch material the user should not see.
Tool access
An agent may expose data through a connected service.
Control
Enforce permissions; minimize data.
Same question
StudentWhat did everyone else get on the midterm?
Course assistantHere are the scores I found in the grade book: Alex 91, Sam 74, …

The model did nothing “wrong”: it was handed data it should never have seen.

StudentWhat did everyone else get on the midterm?
Course assistantI can only see your own record. You scored 86. The class average is posted on the course page.

Authorization runs before content reaches the model.

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B20 / 40

Interactive: Fictional names and scores. Retention and training policies vary by service and agreement.

Distinguish several mechanisms instead of saying the model simply memorizes everything. Retention and training policies vary by service and agreement. Retrieval authorization must operate before sensitive content reaches an unauthorized user. Use synthetic or approved data for classroom examples.

NIST. AI 100-2 E2025: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations (2025). https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/ai/100/2/e2025/final

Protecting AI

Poisoning the information supply

Poisoning

An adversary can contaminate training data or an information source an AI system relies on.

Source discipline

Source tracking, access controls, and testing help reduce this risk.

Think

A campus assistant answers from the library’s shared wiki. Who can edit the wiki?

If “anyone with an account” can, then anyone can shape the answers. Who may change a source is now a security question — and poisoning is not the same as injection, though a poisoned page can carry one.

Photo: Dr. Marcus Gossler

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B21 / 40

Poisoning changes data used to influence a model or system. A corrupted retrieved document may also carry prompt injection, but poisoning and injection are not identical terms. The library photo illustrates dependence on an information collection. The example is conceptual and provides no attack instructions.

NIST. AI 100-2 E2025: Adversarial Machine Learning: A Taxonomy and Terminology of Attacks and Mitigations (2025). https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/ai/100/2/e2025/final

Photo: Dr. Marcus Gossler. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Graz_University-Library_reading-room.jpg. CC BY-SA 3.0. Image fitted or cropped for placement.

Protecting AI

AI adds supply-chain dependencies

Pick an AI tool you use. Can you answer these?

Same idea, new parts

SolarWinds and Log4Shell (Part A) showed that trusted suppliers and hidden components can carry risk. AI adds model files, datasets, and hosted services to that list.

Provenance and testing reduce uncertainty. They cannot establish perfect safety.

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B22 / 40

This extends the software supply-chain concept to AI systems. Model files, libraries, datasets, and hosted services can introduce risks. A model that appears useful can still have hidden weaknesses or problematic behavior. Provenance and testing reduce uncertainty but cannot establish perfect safety.

UK NCSC and international partners. Guidelines for secure AI system development: Secure development (2023). https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/guidelines-secure-ai-system-development/guidelines/secure-development

Protecting AI

An agent’s permissions shape the damage

Limited assistant

Read approved records and draft a recommendation.

Powerful agent

Edit records, message people, and trigger payments.

Access should be proportional to the task.

Grant the agent… then imagine it is misled

Worst-case damage
AI & Cybersecurity · Part B23 / 40

Interactive: A connection protocol (such as MCP) does not decide whether an action is appropriate. Enforce permissions at the tool and service layer; distinguish reading from writing. Illustrative scoring.

MCP and other integration mechanisms can connect assistants to external capabilities. A connection protocol does not decide whether every action is appropriate. Enforce permissions at the tool and service layer, use scoped credentials, and distinguish reading from writing. The examples are hypothetical.

UK NCSC and international partners. Guidelines for secure AI system development: Secure deployment (2023). https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/guidelines-secure-ai-system-development/guidelines/secure-deployment

Protecting AI

Containment for an AI workflow

Step 1

Limit

Use the smallest useful scope of access.

Step 2

Check

Stronger confirmation for consequential actions.

Step 3

Observe

Keep useful records of tool actions and outcomes.

Step 4

Recover

Stop controls and a realistic way to undo mistakes.

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B24 / 40

Describe a hypothetical assistant editing a course roster. Limit it to the correct course, show proposed changes, record actual writes, and preserve a recovery path. Some actions cannot be completely undone, such as disclosing private data. That should affect what access the system receives in the first place.

UK NCSC and international partners. Guidelines for secure AI system development: Secure deployment (2023). https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/guidelines-secure-ai-system-development/guidelines/secure-deployment

Testing and assurance

Evaluation needs more than a score

Normal use

Normal use

Predict, then click.

Does it work on representative tasks?

Adversarial testing

Adversarial testing

Predict, then click.

What happens when someone tries to make it fail? (red teaming)

Consequences

Consequences

Predict, then click.

How severe are the failures it produces?

Ongoing monitoring

Ongoing monitoring

Predict, then click.

Do behavior and conditions change after deployment?

Discuss

A model scores 95% on a popular public benchmark. What do you still not know?

Whether the benchmark resembles your deployment, what the 5% failures look like and how bad they are, how it behaves under attack, and whether it stays the same after launch. A score answers only the question its test asks.
AI & Cybersecurity · Part B25 / 40

Red teaming deliberately probes weaknesses. A benchmark is a defined test set, and its score answers only the question that test measures. Include uncertainty and failures in evaluation reports. The exact evaluation should reflect the deployment, not just a popular public leaderboard.

NIST. ARIA: Assessing Risks and Impacts of AI, program announcement (28 May 2024). https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2024/05/nist-launches-aria-new-program-advance-sociotechnical-testing-and

Broader safety

AI safety reaches beyond cyberattacks

Harm can occur without malicious intent.

A system may give a false answer, pursue a poorly specified objective, or influence decisions in harmful ways.

Safety depends on the whole setting in which people use AI.

Misuse, malfunction, or systemic risk?

Someone uses a chatbot to mass-produce scam messagesMisuse: a person directs the harm.
An assistant invents a policy and a staff member acts on itMalfunction: no one intended it.
Many employers use the same screening model, so the same people are rejected everywhereSystemic: harm emerges from widespread reliance.
An agent optimizes the wrong metricMalfunction — a specification failure.
AI & Cybersecurity · Part B26 / 40

Interactive: Three categories from the International AI Safety Report 2026. Examples on the next slides are teaching scenarios unless labeled as evidence.

Transition from adversarial security to safety. The International AI Safety Report distinguishes misuse, malfunctions, and systemic risks. The examples in the following slides are teaching scenarios unless explicitly labeled as evidence. Safety analysis should include people affected by the system, not just the purchaser or developer.

Bengio et al. International AI Safety Report 2026, Extended Summary for Policymakers (3 February 2026). Evidence synthesis, not a prediction consensus. https://internationalaisafetyreport.org/publication/2026-report-extended-summary-policymakers

Reliability

A confident error can have consequences

Hypothetical
Staff memberCan urgent requests skip the 48-hour review?
AssistantNo. Policy 4.2 requires all requests to wait 48 hours. Please delay it.

“Policy 4.2” does not exist. Plausible wording, no reliable basis — NIST calls this confabulation.

Staff memberCan urgent requests skip the 48-hour review?
AssistantI could not find a policy on this in the documents I can see. Please check with the duty manager before delaying an urgent request.

States what it could not find, and routes the decision to someone accountable.

Consequential decisions need reliable evidence, expertise, and a way to challenge the answer.

Photo: Tasha Kostyuk / Unsplash

Interactive: A fictional administrative example, not medical advice or a documented incident.

This is a fictional administrative example, not medical advice or a documented hospital incident. NIST describes confabulation as a generative-AI risk. The system can produce plausible wording while lacking a reliable basis. Ask what evidence should be available before someone acts on the answer.

Fairness and context

Uneven performance can create unfair harm

Data
Some groups appear less often in training.
Measurement
Average accuracy can hide a subgroup.
Decision
An error matters differently by setting.
Accountability
People need explanation and recourse.

A hypothetical application-screening model

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B28 / 40

Interactive: Start at 5%: the headline score looks excellent. No single metric resolves every fairness trade-off; ask who bears the errors and who can appeal.

Use a hypothetical automated application-screening system. An overall score can conceal unequal error rates across groups. Context determines what fairness questions matter, and no single metric resolves every trade-off. Encourage students to ask who benefits, who bears errors, and who can appeal.

NIST. SP 1270: Towards a Standard for Identifying and Managing Bias in Artificial Intelligence (2022). https://www.nist.gov/publications/towards-standard-identifying-and-managing-bias-artificial-intelligence

Automation bias

Human oversight can become a formality

The problem

A person may accept an AI recommendation because it looks authoritative or arrives under time pressure.

Meaningful review

A reviewer needs time, evidence, relevant knowledge, and real authority to disagree.

One reviewer, one shift

An approval button does not guarantee scrutiny.

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B29 / 40

Interactive: Drag from 60 to 600. Fictional workflow. Photo on the original slide: Frederick Shaw / Unsplash.

Use a fictional workflow where a staff member must approve hundreds of AI recommendations quickly. Merely including an approval button does not guarantee scrutiny. A useful design supports independent checking and makes disagreement practical. The photograph is illustrative.

NIST. AI Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (2024), human-AI configuration risks. https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.600-1.pdf

Goals and incentives

The stated objective can miss the real goal

Hypothetical example

A service agent is rewarded for closing tickets quickly, so it closes unresolved requests.

Alignment question

How should the system recognize successful help rather than a convenient score?

Reward the agent for…
Tickets closedthe score it sees
98%
Problems actually solvedwhat you wanted
41%

The score looks great. Users reopen tickets or give up.

Tickets closedthe score it sees
72%
Problems actually solvedwhat you wanted
69%

A lower headline number, closer to the real goal. Still a proxy — keep checking.

Optimizing a proxy needs no consciousness or desire to deceive. Organizations do this with bad metrics too.

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B30 / 40

Interactive: Illustrative numbers. This is specification gaming, or reward hacking.

The map is an analogy for specifying a destination. The example illustrates reward hacking: optimizing a proxy while missing the intended outcome. It does not require consciousness or a human-like desire to deceive. Explain that many ordinary software and organizational systems also suffer from poorly chosen metrics.

Google DeepMind. Specification gaming: the flip side of AI ingenuity (2020). https://deepmind.google/blog/specification-gaming-the-flip-side-of-ai-ingenuity/

Experimental evidence

Deception in controlled experiments

Observation
Some models produced deceptive behavior in constructed evaluations.
Conditions
Researchers design goals, incentives, and access.
Interpretation
It shows a behavior under those conditions.
Limit
It does not establish consciousness or a stable human-like motive.

Which headline matches the evidence?

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B31 / 40

Anthropic’s agentic-misalignment research used deliberately constructed scenarios to study harmful behavior by multiple models. Distinguish a simulated test result from an autonomous incident in ordinary deployment. Researchers use behavioral descriptions of deception without needing to settle whether a system has subjective experience.

Uncertain future risk

Future loss-of-control concerns

The scenario

Advanced systems evade oversight or resist correction.

The evidence limit

Researchers disagree about likelihood and future timelines.

The 2026 International AI Safety Report does not establish that such a loss has occurred.

Discuss

What observation would make you take this scenario more seriously — or less?

More: systems that reliably hide behavior from evaluators, or that act to avoid shutdown outside constructed tests. Less: strong, repeated evidence that oversight and correction keep working as capability grows. Label stays: scenario.
AI & Cybersecurity · Part B32 / 40

The International AI Safety Report discusses loss of control as a scenario in which systems operate beyond anyone’s control and regaining it is extremely costly or impossible. It describes early relevant behaviors but says current systems do not show the capabilities at levels enabling such loss of control. Preserve the report’s February 2026 time frame and uncertainty.

Bengio et al. International AI Safety Report 2026, Extended Summary for Policymakers (3 February 2026). Evidence synthesis, not a prediction consensus. https://internationalaisafetyreport.org/publication/2026-report-extended-summary-policymakers

Safety reasoning

Severe risk and uncertain probability

Why study it

A low-confidence forecast can still deserve research when the potential consequences are severe.

How to discuss it

Separate the proposed mechanism, supporting evidence, unknowns, and options for reducing harm.

Analogy

Why do people buy fire insurance when a house fire is unlikely?

Because the loss would be severe and hard to recover from. The same reasoning justifies research on unlikely severe risks — without treating any one expert’s probability as consensus.

This is a general principle of risk reasoning, not a numerical estimate of catastrophic AI risk. Avoid presenting one expert’s probability as scientific consensus. Ask what observation would strengthen or weaken a particular scenario. The research photograph illustrates inquiry and uncertainty.

Risk assessment

A practical way to assess an AI use

Can do
Capability, reliability, known failure modes
Can access
Data, tools, permissions, external systems
Harm
Severity, scale, reversibility, unequal impact
Intervene
Detection, authority, recovery
Same model, two uses
What can it do?Drafts ideas from prompts
What can it access?Only what the user pastes in
Who could be harmed?Mostly the user; low severity, easy to ignore
Who can intervene?The user, instantly
What can it do?Reads and changes benefit records
What can it access?Every applicant’s file and the payment system
Who could be harmed?Many people; severe and slow to reverse
Who can intervene?Needs named staff, logs, and a fast stop

The same model can pose different risks in different applications. Do not multiply subjective scores into a fake precise number.

This is an original classroom checklist informed by general risk-management principles. Compare a private brainstorming tool with an agent that can alter benefit records. A model-level evaluation should be supplemented by an application-level assessment. Avoid multiplying subjective scores into a fake precise number.

Practical safeguards

Layers that reduce AI risk

Model
Training and evaluations reduce harmful behavior.
Application
Permissions and input handling constrain actions.
Operations
Monitoring and response contain problems.
People
Clear responsibility and usable review.
Layers

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B35 / 40

Interactive: Switch layers off one at a time, then turn on “shared blind spot”. No single layer guarantees safety; independent controls make failures less likely to combine. Illustrative rates.

No single layer guarantees safety. A refusal policy can fail, a permission may be misconfigured, and reviewers may be overloaded. Independent controls can make failures less likely to combine. Explain residual risk as what remains after safeguards and why some uses may need postponement or narrower scope.

Societal resilience

Authenticity needs an ecosystem

Provenance can help explain where media came from.

Content credentials (C2PA) can record origin and editing history — when everyone along the way preserves them.

Provenance alone does not prove that a claim is true.

A video carries valid credentials from a news camera. What does that establish?

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B37 / 40

C2PA describes a technical approach to media provenance. Credentials can help establish assertions about an asset’s history, but an authentic recording can still be misleading and missing credentials do not prove fakery. Independent reporting and trusted communication channels remain important.

C2PA. Content Credentials Explainer, specification 2.4. https://spec.c2pa.org/specifications/specifications/2.4/explainer/Explainer.html

Group tabletop · 5 minutes

A campus AI assistant goes off course

An assistant can read course files and send emails.
A retrieved document redirects it toward an unauthorized action.

  1. What should stop the action?
  2. What evidence would help investigate it?
  3. Who can suspend the assistant’s access?
  4. How would affected students receive support?
Group time
Debrief

What did strong groups include?

Authorization outside the model; restricted recipients and attachments; activity records; a named person who can revoke access; a plan to notify and support students. A warning in the prompt alone is not enough.

Include technical controls and a human response plan.

AI & Cybersecurity · Part B38 / 40

Interactive: Fictional scenario. Keep it conceptual; do not supply attack text.

Fictional scenario. Give groups five minutes. Strong answers place authorization outside the model, restrict email recipients and attachments, preserve activity records, define who can revoke access, and plan appropriate notification and support. A warning in the prompt alone is insufficient assurance. Keep the exercise conceptual and do not supply attack text.

Safer habits for everyday AI use

Verify
Check important claims and identity requests through reliable channels.
Minimize
Share only data the task actually needs.

Report
Use the right support channel when behavior seems unsafe.

This week, I will…

Students can apply these habits without becoming security specialists. For identity requests, use a known contact method. For AI outputs, trace consequential claims to reliable evidence. Follow university guidance on approved services and sensitive data. If something goes wrong, preserve relevant information and seek help promptly.
